result:
result: No blocking gaps. Every directive of the removed skill and both role sections is carried into text the visual agents read. Two non-blocking issues: the attribution wording overstates "paraphrased", and some text is duplicated. Read-only, no shell: I checked by reading the sources and by Grep, and ran no gates. The dist files are in step with the sources for the phrases I sampled.

blocking: none.

non-blocking:
1. `docs/attributions.md:22` says "No text was copied from any of them", but several new passages stay close to the original frontend-design wording. These are the hero paragraph and "default hero" sentence (`web-design/SKILL.md:19`), the "Type carries the page's personality … clearly distinct" sentence and the Elements of Typographic Style clause (`:20`), the SaaS-card kit and template-chrome lists with the same hex values (`:67`, `:75`, `:76`), and the motion sentence (`:54`). Core `core.md:14`, `:16`, `:37`, `:42`–`:45` also track the original closely. With the Apache-2.0 license file removed, this is the weak point. Smallest fix: reword those passages further, or soften the sentence to "restated in this project's own words, with ideas from the sources below". Do not claim "no text copied" for the `frontend-design` row.
2. `docs/attributions.md:22`: "embedded … until 0.2.2" is ambiguous, because `package.json` is at 0.2.2 now. Say "before 0.2.2" or "through 0.2.1" once you confirm which release last shipped it.
3. Weakened directives, all minor:
   - Confirming a proposed subject with the client is now only "propose them in the plan" (`core.md:13`).
   - The "no need for a separate display and body typeface" permission is gone.
   - The "conversational" tone cue is gone.
   - The "balance what you're good at against experimenting" sentence is gone.
   - Smallest fix: add "and confirm with the client where one is reachable" to `core.md:13`. The rest can stay.
4. Duplication:
   - The content list "shared core (direction before code, the plan, copy, the quality floor), platform rules, refuse list, capture checklist" appears in `worker-visual/design.md:3` and `visual-judging/SKILL.md:13`. Keep it in one place.
   - "01 / 02 / 03" numbering is stated in both `core.md:36` and `web-design/SKILL.md:73`.
   - The eyebrow and label rule appears in both `core.md:36` and `web-design/SKILL.md:68`.
   - The reduced-motion rule appears in both `core.md:51` and `web-design/SKILL.md:56`.
5. When no skill is named, the agents only report that none was named (`worker-visual/design.md:3`, `reviewer-visual/design.md:3`). Previously they always had the embedded guidance. This is an intended design; `visual-judging` makes the root name the skill. A fallback is optional.
6. Only `web-design` carries the hero, typography, motion and tell lists. The shared core carries the rest to all four design skills, which is reasonable for a web-origin source.

Criterion 1 (directives carried) is met, with the minor losses in item 3. Criterion 3 (agents still told which skill to load) is met: both `design.md` files tell them to read the skill file their criteria name and judge or build against its checklist. Criterion 5 (no stale mentions) is met: Grep finds `frontend-design` only in the credit (`README.md:47`, `docs/attributions.md:22` and `:26`) and the removal test (`plugin.test.ts:171`). The vendor folder, license and the `dist` skill and license files are gone, and the remaining "vendor" hits concern ripgrep and fd.
